package harness

// Runtime tests for scg-generated Go code. internal/gen/runtime_test.go
// generates testdata/runtime/schema into a temporary module, copies this file
// next to it and runs `go test` there.
//
// To fuzz manually: copy the module the test prints with -v, then run
// `go test -fuzz FuzzFromBytes`.

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/json"
	"math/rand"
	"reflect"
	"runtime"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/google/uuid"
	"github.com/kbirk/scg/pkg/serialize"

	"scgharness/gen/rt"
)

type message interface {
	BitSize() int
	Serialize(*serialize.Writer)
	Deserialize(*serialize.Reader) error
	ToBytes() []byte
	FromBytes([]byte) error
}

// allocated returns the bytes allocated while running f. TotalAlloc is
// monotonic, so no GC is needed.
func allocated(f func()) uint64 {
	var before, after runtime.MemStats
	runtime.ReadMemStats(&before)
	f()
	runtime.ReadMemStats(&after)
	return after.TotalAlloc - before.TotalAlloc
}

func hostileFrame(count uint32, payload []byte) []byte {
	w := serialize.NewWriter(8)
	serialize.SerializeUInt32(w, count)
	w.WriteBytes(payload)
	return w.Bytes()
}

// A list<Big> frame declaring as many elements as it has bytes: each Big is at
// least 268 bits (8 strings, 2 timestamps, 2 uuids), so the length is impossible and must be rejected before the
// ~208 bytes per element are preallocated (previously 1 MiB -> 208 MiB).
func TestHostileListLengthIsRejectedBeforeAllocating(t *testing.T) {
	payload := make([]byte, 1<<20)
	frame := hostileFrame(uint32(len(payload)+5), payload)

	var err error
	n := allocated(func() {
		var m rt.ListBig
		err = m.FromBytes(frame)
	})
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatal("expected an error for an impossible list length")
	}
	if n > 1<<20 {
		t.Fatalf("decoding a 1 MiB frame allocated %d bytes", n)
	}

	n = allocated(func() {
		var m rt.MapBig
		err = m.FromBytes(frame)
	})
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatal("expected an error for an impossible map length")
	}
	if n > 1<<20 {
		t.Fatalf("decoding a 1 MiB frame allocated %d bytes", n)
	}
}

// A plausible length followed by garbage: the length passes the minimum-size
// check, so the preallocation must stay within the budget (16x the frame).
func TestPlausibleListLengthPreallocationIsBounded(t *testing.T) {
	payload := make([]byte, 256<<10)
	rand.New(rand.NewSource(1)).Read(payload)
	count := uint32(len(payload) * 8 / 268)
	frame := hostileFrame(count, payload)

	n := allocated(func() {
		var m rt.ListBig
		_ = m.FromBytes(frame)
	})
	if limit := uint64(16*len(frame) + (1 << 20)); n > limit {
		t.Fatalf("decoding a %d byte frame allocated %d bytes (limit %d)", len(frame), n, limit)
	}
}

func TestLargeLegitimateListsRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	big := rt.ListBig{}
	for i := 0; i < 10000; i++ {
		big.Items = append(big.Items, rt.Big{S0: "x", U0: uuid.New(), T0: time.Unix(int64(i), 0)})
	}
	var decoded rt.ListBig
	if err := decoded.FromBytes(big.ToBytes()); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(decoded.Items) != 10000 || decoded.Items[9999].U0 != big.Items[9999].U0 {
		t.Fatal("list<Big> did not round trip")
	}

	ints := rt.ListInt{Items: make([]int32, 200000)}
	for i := range ints.Items {
		ints.Items[i] = int32(i * 7)
	}
	var decodedInts rt.ListInt
	if err := decodedInts.FromBytes(ints.ToBytes()); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(ints.Items, decodedInts.Items) {
		t.Fatal("list<int32> did not round trip")
	}
}

// list<byte> / list<uint8> are (de)serialized in bulk; the encoding must be
// identical to the element-by-element encoding of a uint32 count followed by
// one SerializeUInt8 per element, including at an unaligned bit offset.
func TestByteListsAreWireIdenticalToElementwiseEncoding(t *testing.T) {
	for _, n := range []int{0, 1, 7, 8, 9, 300, 4096} {
		data := make([]byte, n)
		rand.New(rand.NewSource(int64(n))).Read(data)
		m := rt.Bytes{Misalign: true, Data: data, More: data, Nested: [][]byte{data, {}, data}}

		w := serialize.NewWriter(0)
		serialize.SerializeBool(w, true)
		elementwise := func(bs []byte) {
			serialize.SerializeUInt32(w, uint32(len(bs)))
			for _, b := range bs {
				serialize.SerializeUInt8(w, b)
			}
		}
		elementwise(data)
		elementwise(data)
		serialize.SerializeUInt32(w, 3)
		elementwise(data)
		elementwise([]byte{})
		elementwise(data)

		if !bytes.Equal(m.ToBytes(), w.Bytes()) {
			t.Fatalf("n=%d: bulk byte list encoding differs from the elementwise encoding", n)
		}
		if serialize.BitsToBytes(m.BitSize()) != len(w.Bytes()) {
			t.Fatalf("n=%d: BitSize disagrees with the encoded length", n)
		}

		var decoded rt.Bytes
		if err := decoded.FromBytes(w.Bytes()); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if !bytes.Equal(decoded.Data, data) || !bytes.Equal(decoded.More, data) || len(decoded.Nested) != 3 {
			t.Fatalf("n=%d: byte lists did not round trip", n)
		}
		if decoded.Nested[1] == nil {
			t.Fatal("an empty byte list must decode to a non-nil slice, as before")
		}
	}
}

func TestByteListLengthIsBounded(t *testing.T) {
	w := serialize.NewWriter(0)
	serialize.SerializeBool(w, true) // misalign
	serialize.SerializeUInt32(w, 1<<30)
	w.WriteBytes(make([]byte, 64))
	frame := w.Bytes()
	var m rt.Bytes
	n := allocated(func() {
		if err := m.FromBytes(frame); err == nil {
			t.Fatal("expected an error")
		}
	})
	if n > 1<<20 {
		t.Fatalf("allocated %d bytes", n)
	}
}

// randomFill populates v with random data, recursively.
func randomFill(r *rand.Rand, v reflect.Value, depth int) {
	switch v.Kind() {
	case reflect.Bool:
		v.SetBool(r.Intn(2) == 1)
	case reflect.Int8, reflect.Int16, reflect.Int32, reflect.Int64:
		bits := v.Type().Bits()
		x := r.Int63()
		if r.Intn(2) == 0 {
			x = -x
		}
		if r.Intn(3) == 0 {
			x = int64(r.Intn(5)) - 2
		}
		v.SetInt(x >> (64 - bits))
	case reflect.Uint8, reflect.Uint16, reflect.Uint32, reflect.Uint64:
		bits := v.Type().Bits()
		x := r.Uint64()
		if r.Intn(3) == 0 {
			x = uint64(r.Intn(3))
		}
		if v.Type().Name() == "Kind" {
			v.SetUint(uint64(r.Intn(3)))
			return
		}
		v.SetUint(x >> (64 - bits))
	case reflect.Float32, reflect.Float64:
		v.SetFloat(r.NormFloat64() * 1e6)
	case reflect.String:
		b := make([]byte, r.Intn(12))
		r.Read(b)
		v.SetString(string(b))
	case reflect.Array:
		for i := 0; i < v.Len(); i++ {
			randomFill(r, v.Index(i), depth+1)
		}
	case reflect.Slice:
		if depth > 3 {
			v.Set(reflect.MakeSlice(v.Type(), 0, 0))
			return
		}
		n := r.Intn(5)
		s := reflect.MakeSlice(v.Type(), n, n)
		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
			randomFill(r, s.Index(i), depth+1)
		}
		v.Set(s)
	case reflect.Map:
		n := r.Intn(4)
		if depth > 3 {
			n = 0
		}
		m := reflect.MakeMapWithSize(v.Type(), n)
		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
			k := reflect.New(v.Type().Key()).Elem()
			randomFill(r, k, depth+1)
			e := reflect.New(v.Type().Elem()).Elem()
			randomFill(r, e, depth+1)
			m.SetMapIndex(k, e)
		}
		v.Set(m)
	case reflect.Struct:
		if v.Type() == reflect.TypeOf(time.Time{}) {
			sec := r.Int63n(4_000_000_000) - 2_000_000_000
			v.Set(reflect.ValueOf(time.Unix(sec, r.Int63n(1_000_000_000))))
			return
		}
		for i := 0; i < v.NumField(); i++ {
			if v.Field(i).CanSet() {
				randomFill(r, v.Field(i), depth+1)
			}
		}
	}
}

// equal compares decoded values, treating times by instant.
func equal(a, b reflect.Value) bool {
	if a.Type() == reflect.TypeOf(time.Time{}) {
		return a.Interface().(time.Time).Equal(b.Interface().(time.Time))
	}
	switch a.Kind() {
	case reflect.Struct:
		for i := 0; i < a.NumField(); i++ {
			if !equal(a.Field(i), b.Field(i)) {
				return false
			}
		}
		return true
	case reflect.Slice, reflect.Array:
		if a.Len() != b.Len() {
			return false
		}
		for i := 0; i < a.Len(); i++ {
			if !equal(a.Index(i), b.Index(i)) {
				return false
			}
		}
		return true
	case reflect.Map:
		if a.Len() != b.Len() {
			return false
		}
		for _, k := range a.MapKeys() {
			bv := b.MapIndex(k)
			if !bv.IsValid() || !equal(a.MapIndex(k), bv) {
				return false
			}
		}
		return true
	case reflect.Float32, reflect.Float64:
		return a.Float() == b.Float()
	}
	return reflect.DeepEqual(a.Interface(), b.Interface())
}

// BitSize must equal the number of bits Serialize writes. Serializing after k
// leading bits (k = 0..7) and checking the byte length catches any off-by-n,
// and decoding checks that Deserialize consumes exactly those bits.
func TestBitSizeEqualsBitsWritten(t *testing.T) {
	r := rand.New(rand.NewSource(42))
	for iter := 0; iter < 300; iter++ {
		var m rt.Everything
		randomFill(r, reflect.ValueOf(&m).Elem(), 0)
		size := m.BitSize()
		for k := 0; k < 8; k++ {
			w := serialize.NewWriter(0)
			for i := 0; i < k; i++ {
				serialize.SerializeBool(w, true)
			}
			m.Serialize(w)
			serialize.SerializeBool(w, true) // trailing marker
			if got, want := len(w.Bytes()), serialize.BitsToBytes(k+size+1); got != want {
				t.Fatalf("iteration %d, offset %d: wrote %d bytes, BitSize %d implies %d", iter, k, got, size, want)
			}

			reader := serialize.NewReader(w.Bytes())
			for i := 0; i < k; i++ {
				var b bool
				if err := serialize.DeserializeBool(&b, reader); err != nil || !b {
					t.Fatal("bad prefix")
				}
			}
			var decoded rt.Everything
			if err := decoded.Deserialize(reader); err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("iteration %d: %v", iter, err)
			}
			var marker bool
			if err := serialize.DeserializeBool(&marker, reader); err != nil || !marker {
				t.Fatalf("iteration %d, offset %d: Deserialize did not consume exactly the bits written", iter, k)
			}
			if k == 0 && !equal(reflect.ValueOf(m), reflect.ValueOf(decoded)) {
				t.Fatalf("iteration %d: round trip mismatch", iter)
			}
		}
	}
}

func decodeTargets() []func() message {
	return []func() message{
		func() message { return &rt.Everything{} },
		func() message { return &rt.ListBig{} },
		func() message { return &rt.MapBig{} },
		func() message { return &rt.Bytes{} },
		func() message { return &rt.ListInt{} },
	}
}

// checkDecode decodes arbitrary input into every message type: it must never
// panic, and must stay within an allocation budget proportional to the input.
func checkDecode(t *testing.T, input []byte) {
	for _, newMsg := range decodeTargets() {
		m := newMsg()
		n := allocated(func() {
			_ = m.FromBytes(input)
		})
		if limit := uint64(64*len(input) + (1 << 20)); n > limit {
			t.Fatalf("%T: decoding %d bytes allocated %d (limit %d)", m, len(input), n, limit)
		}
	}
}

func seedInputs() [][]byte {
	r := rand.New(rand.NewSource(7))
	var seeds [][]byte
	for i := 0; i < 20; i++ {
		var m rt.Everything
		randomFill(r, reflect.ValueOf(&m).Elem(), 0)
		bs := m.ToBytes()
		seeds = append(seeds, bs, bs[:len(bs)/2])
	}
	seeds = append(seeds, []byte{}, []byte{0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff})
	return seeds
}

func TestRandomInputsDoNotPanicOrOverAllocate(t *testing.T) {
	r := rand.New(rand.NewSource(99))
	for _, seed := range seedInputs() {
		checkDecode(t, seed)
		// mutate valid encodings, the most interesting inputs
		for i := 0; i < 20 && len(seed) > 0; i++ {
			mutated := append([]byte(nil), seed...)
			for j := 0; j < 1+r.Intn(4); j++ {
				mutated[r.Intn(len(mutated))] = byte(r.Intn(256))
			}
			checkDecode(t, mutated)
		}
	}
	for i := 0; i < 200; i++ {
		b := make([]byte, r.Intn(64))
		r.Read(b)
		checkDecode(t, b)
	}
}

func FuzzFromBytes(f *testing.F) {
	for _, seed := range seedInputs() {
		f.Add(seed)
	}
	f.Fuzz(func(t *testing.T, input []byte) {
		checkDecode(t, input)
	})
}

// uuid typedefs encode like uuid.UUID: a canonical string, usable as a JSON
// map key, while still accepting the array of 16 numbers that earlier
// generated code wrote.
func TestUUIDTypedefJSON(t *testing.T) {
	id := rt.ID(uuid.MustParse("6ba7b810-9dad-11d1-80b4-00c04fd430c8"))

	bs, err := json.Marshal(id)
	if err != nil || string(bs) != `"6ba7b810-9dad-11d1-80b4-00c04fd430c8"` {
		t.Fatalf("Marshal: %s %v", bs, err)
	}

	m := rt.Everything{TypedID: id, ByID: map[rt.ID]rt.Big{id: {S0: "x"}}}
	text, err := m.ToJSON()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ToJSON with a uuid typedef map key: %v", err)
	}
	if !bytes.Contains(text, []byte(`"by_id":{"6ba7b810-9dad-11d1-80b4-00c04fd430c8":`)) {
		t.Fatalf("unexpected JSON: %s", text)
	}
	var decoded rt.Everything
	if err := decoded.FromJSON(text); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if decoded.TypedID != id || decoded.ByID[id].S0 != "x" {
		t.Fatal("uuid typedef did not round trip through JSON")
	}

	// the legacy encoding: an array of 16 numbers
	legacy, _ := json.Marshal([16]byte(id))
	var fromLegacy rt.ID
	if err := json.Unmarshal(legacy, &fromLegacy); err != nil || fromLegacy != id {
		t.Fatalf("legacy array form: %v", err)
	}

	// null is a no-op, as for other types
	keep := id
	if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte("null"), &keep); err != nil || keep != id {
		t.Fatalf("null: %v", err)
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(`"not-a-uuid"`), &keep); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("expected an error")
	}
}
